Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.
data.title: Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight raises with the card; raise slider max 180 / default 60

## Summary

Research spike to determine the client-side follow-detection mechanism for the "Follow us on Steam" incentive. The Steam client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call, so candidates must be verified before committing. This feature produces the decision-gate report that F4 depends on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A report documents and evaluates each candidate: `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account>)` (client-side, no backend), Steam Web API `IPlayerService` (game-page follow, needs server + publisher API key), and any other client-side candidates discovered.
- [ ] The report states a recommendation and flags the UX impact of each candidate (e.g. follows developer account vs game page).
- [ ] The recommendation is confirmed with the user (decision gate) and recorded in this item before F4 implementation commits to a mechanism.
- [ ] Any unknown (e.g. whether a server component is acceptable) is surfaced as an open question with options, not silently assumed.

## Minimal Implementation

- Prototype a minimal probe using the Steamworks SDK against a real Steam account (dev environment with Steam running).
- Research Steamworks SDK docs / community reports for `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` semantics.
- Write findings to the work item as a structured report (markdown), including a decision recommendation.
- No production code committed in this feature.

## Prototype/Experiment

Success = a clear recommendation with evidence (docs/community/experiment) that the implementer can act on without re-research.

## Dependencies

- Parent blocked-by CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (Electron launcher) — launcher must exist to run Steamworks in-app.

## Deliverables

- Decision-gate report (in work item comments).
- Confirmed mechanism choice.
data.title: F1: Follow-detection mechanism research spike

Test-first contract for the follow-source interface and unlock/persistence logic using a mocked Steamworks session, written before the implementation features (F3/F4). Defines the interface the renderer and unlock logic consume so the Steam SDK stays behind an abstraction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A mockable `FollowSource` interface is defined (init, isSteamAvailable, openStorePage, isFollowing, claim) with a deterministic fake implementation.
- [ ] Unit tests (`tests/steam-follow/`) cover: follow detected → unlock flow triggered; already-unlocked → no re-verification prompt; Steam absent → graceful degraded path (no crash); choose-one-of-three catalog resolution; unlock persistence round-trip across simulated launches.
- [ ] Tests run and pass under `--project unit` (fast, no browser).
- [ ] The interface contract documents that the renderer never imports the Steam SDK directly.

## Minimal Implementation

- Test-only feature: interface + test doubles + unit tests.
- Reference the launcher item's content-locator abstraction (CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW) for the dependency-injection pattern.

## Dependencies

- Parent blocked-by CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (launcher) for the abstraction pattern it establishes.

## Summary

Operator-run end-to-end verification on a real Steam account that automatic follow detection unlocks the bonus game, plus a graceful-degradation re-check. Satisfies parent AC2.

**Status: awaiting operator execution (2026-09-30).** The agent cannot run this: it needs a **Windows x64 host with a real Steam client and account**, which is not provisioned in the agent environment. Per the producer, do **not** assume the client is logged in — verify both the logged-in automatic path and the not-logged-in / Steam-absent fallbacks. The implementation (P1–P5) is complete and pushed to `dev`; `docs/dev/steam-follow-qa.md` is updated with the automatic-detection path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With the addon built into the package and Steam **logged in**, `SteamworksFollowSource.followCheckSupported` becomes `true` on a real Steam session and automatic unlock is verified end-to-end (designated bonus unlocked, no manual claim).
- [ ] With the addon present but **no user logged in**, the launcher does not crash, `isFollowing` returns `false`, the bonus stays locked, and the manual claim remains available (no fabricated follow).
- [ ] The unlock persists across a relaunch without re-verification.
- [ ] With Steam absent, the launcher boots, the bonus stays locked, and every non-gated game remains playable (no crash).
- [ ] Evidence (screenshots/notes) is recorded and the known-limitation note in `docs/dev/steam-follow-qa.md` is removed or updated (already rewritten in P5; confirm on the real build).
- [ ] Parent `CG-0MUN7930Y009X8Z1` AC2 is satisfied.

## Operator Steps

1. On Windows x64: `npm install steamworks.js && npm run build:steam-friends && npm run package:steam`.
2. Execute `docs/dev/steam-follow-qa.md` (sections 1–6), recording Pass/Fail/N/A and evidence per step.
3. Record the results as a comment on this item.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by P4 and P5 (both complete).

## Deliverables

- QA evidence comment + any QA-document corrections found on the real build.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/steam-follow-qa.md`

# Create the Steamworks project for Tableau Card Engine

External producer action (Steamworks partner backend). The achievement work for
Main Street (and the other TCE games) maps challenge completions to persistent
Steam achievements, but no Steamworks project/App ID exists yet — so the
matching achievement API names cannot be registered.

## Goal / user story

As the Tableau Card Engine producer, I need a Steamworks project (App ID) for
the game so that achievements can be registered and unlocked for real players.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A Steamworks partner project exists for Tableau Card Engine and has an assigned App ID.
2. The App ID is recorded somewhere version-controlled (launcher config or documented env/config) so `steamworks.js` can initialise against it.
3. The producer account can access the project's achievement configuration in the Steamworks partner backend.

## Constraints

- Producer/external action — not implementable by a code agent.
- Must be completed before the achievement-registration item (see dependency below).

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ**: Challenges as achievements: sync in-game challenges to Steam achievements (epic)
- **MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7**: Serial Seller: achievement manifest entry + Steamworks API name (blocking consumer)

# Provision the private Steam config for the TCE launcher

Producer/external action. The Steam follow-to-unlock incentive
(`CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC`) and the Steam achievements work
(`CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ`) need real Steam credentials on the QA machine before
their real-Steam end-to-end verification can run. These values are private and
must never be committed.

## Goal / user story

As the TCE producer, I need the launcher's private Steam config provisioned on
the QA machine so the launcher can initialise against the real Steamworks
project and the follow-detection check can be exercised end-to-end.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The private Steam config is present on the QA machine, either as environment
   variables (`TCE_STEAM_APP_ID`, `TCE_STEAM_DEVELOPER_STEAM_ID`) or as a
   gitignored `electron/steam-config.local.json` matching
   `electron/steam-config.example.json`.
2. The values are the real Steamworks App ID and the developer account
   SteamID64; they are **not** committed to any repository and are not pasted
   into worklog comments.
3. The launcher reads the config successfully on a Windows Steam build
   (`npm run build:steam-friends && npm run package:steam`).

## Constraints

- Producer/external action — cannot be completed by a code agent on the Linux
  build host; it requires the private Steamworks partner credentials.
- The upstream Steamworks project/App ID creation is tracked by
  `CG-0MUPMJVS90019KSQ`.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC** — Follow-on-Steam incentive (blocked by this item).
- **CG-0MUPMJVS90019KSQ** — Create the Steamworks project for Tableau Card Engine (supplies the App ID).
- **CG-0MUOC5OV4006OTLG** / **CG-0MUNBI08A001D0XU** — real-Steam end-to-end verification that consumes this config.
- `docs/dev/steam-follow-qa.md` — manual QA plan; `electron/steam-config.example.json` — config shape.

# Intake Brief — Cutting a release from a game uses the TCE version number

**Work item:** CG-0MVGF2QE9008NA5R — Cutting a release from a game uses the TCE version number

## Problem statement

When a release is cut from a game repo such as `tce-main-street`, the game ends up versioned with the Tableau-Card-Engine (core) version number. Each game repo must maintain its **own** independent version, decoupled from the core's release cadence.

## Users / user stories

- **Game maintainers (agents + operators)** cutting a release of a sibling game repo:
  "As a maintainer of `tce-main-street`, I want the game's release version to reflect the
  game's own release history, so players can tell the game version apart from the engine version."
- **Players and testers** reading the version label on the game selector / game screens:
  "As a playtester, I want the version I report in feedback to identify the game build
  (and be meaningful on its own), not silently mirror the engine version."
- **Engine maintainers** composing the multi-repo distribution:
  "As an engine maintainer, I want a game's release version to be independent of the
  engine's, so engine releases and game releases can proceed at different cadences."

## Root-cause analysis (evidence)

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `renderPackageJson()` writes the game repo's
  `package.json` with `version: manifest.version ?? '0.0.0'`, where `manifest` is the
  **core's** `package.json` (`readCoreManifest(coreRoot)`). A new or re-scaffolded game
  therefore inherits the core's current version number.
- The behaviour is pinned by a test: `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`
  asserts `expect(pkg.version).toBe('9.9.9')` (the stubbed core manifest version).
- Observed in the wild: every `tce-*` sibling carries a core-derived version —
  0.1.17 for the batch scaffolded 2026-09-26 (the core version at that date), and
  0.1.21 for `main-street` / `the-rising`, whose releases tracked the core's version
  patch-for-patch (core v0.1.17→v0.1.21, main-street v0.1.17→v0.1.21).
- **Not the cause:** the ship skill's `bump-version.js` resolves the **invoking repo's**
  root via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and bumps that `package.json`, so once a
  game repo carries its own version its releases bump correctly. The coupling is
  seeded at scaffold time and then persists.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No core-version coupling in the scaffold.** `renderPackageJson()` no longer derives
   the game's version from the core manifest: a freshly scaffolded game repo's
   `package.json` `version` is the independent baseline `0.1.0` (producer decision), and
   a re-scaffold of an existing game repo **preserves** the version already in that
   repo's `package.json` rather than overwriting it.
2. **Existing game repos are not renumbered.** The work does not rewrite sibling game
   repo versions: `golf` / `blackjack` / `coloretto` / `feudalism` / `lost-cities` /
   `sushi-go` / `beleaguered-castle` (0.1.17), `the-rising` (0.1.21) and `main-street`
   (0.1.21) keep their current numbers and diverge naturally on their next release.
   A re-scaffold of any of them is version-neutral (verified for at least one repo, or
   covered by the unit-test preserve case).
3. **Scope limited to the scaffold seeding path, with the ship path verified.** Only the
   scaffold seeding + its tests/docs change; a verification note records that the ship
   `bump-version.js` reads the invoking repo's own `package.json` (no shared/release-code
   change required). Any newly discovered version-leak path is filed as a follow-up work
   item rather than folded into this one.
4. **Tests.** Unit tests cover: (a) a new-game scaffold seeds `0.1.0`; (b) a re-scaffold
   of an existing repo preserves its version; (c) no test asserts core-version coupling
   (the `'9.9.9'` assertion is replaced). Tests must exercise real `package.json`
   read/write behaviour, not merely assert rendered strings in isolation.
5. **Documentation.** The per-game version policy is documented (each game owns its
   version; the scaffold seeds `0.1.0` and preserves on re-scaffold; a game release bumps
   only that game's version) in the new-game guide and/or the multi-repo architecture
   scaffold section.
6. **Quality gates.** `npm test -- --project unit` and `npm run build` pass with the
   change; all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Do not edit the global ship skill or any `skill/` tree (`AGENTS.md` repository
  boundary); the bump logic is already repo-local and needs verification only.
- Push to `dev` only. Cross-repo game changes (if any) are recorded on this core work
  item or in the game repo's own Worklog store.
- `renderPackageJson` stays a pure render function: the preserve-on-re-scaffold decision
  must be injected/explicit (e.g. an existing-version parameter or a read in
  `scaffoldGameRepo`), keeping the template unit-testable.
- Do not add a hard-coded per-game version table — the policy is generic.

## Existing state

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` is the single generator for every `tce-<game>` repo
  `package.json`; it is invoked via `npm run scaffold:game` / `scaffold:games` (core),
  `npm run scaffold` (game repos) and `scripts/setup-distribution.ts`.
- `ScaffoldOptions` carries `coreManifest?: CoreManifest`; `CoreManifest.version` is
  typed optional and only used for the game version stamp.
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` has a `renderPackageJson` describe block
  and a `scaffoldGameRepo` integration block using a temp sibling layout.
- Game repos carry `__APP_VERSION__` injected from **their own** `package.json` in their
  `vite.config.ts` (generated by the same scaffold), so display follows the package
  version automatically once seeding is fixed.
- `configs/engine-pin.json` in each game repo records the engine **commit** (not a
  version), so engine/game version independence has no other data coupling.

## Desired change

- Seed a new game repo at `0.1.0`; preserve an existing repo's version on re-scaffold.
- Keep `renderPackageJson` pure and explicit about the version it writes.
- Replace the core-version-coupling test with baseline + preserve coverage.
- Document the per-game version policy (who owns a game's version, how a release bumps
  it, and why it is not the engine version).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `renderPackageJson()` (drop `manifest.version`; take an explicit version), `ScaffoldOptions`, `scaffoldGameRepo()` (read the existing `package.json` version before writing).
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — replace `expect(pkg.version).toBe('9.9.9')` with baseline + preserve cases; add a re-scaffold integration case against a temp repo with an existing version.
- `docs/dev/creating-a-new-game.md` — §3 scaffold stage: state the seeded baseline and that games own their version.
- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` — §5 "Per-game repo scaffold": version-ownership note alongside the existing `package.json` description.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Build-Time Version Injection: clarify the label shows the **composing repo's** version (game repo ⇒ game version, core ⇒ engine version).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — re-scaffold clobbers a released version.** If the preserve path reads the
  wrong file or a stale path, a re-scaffold could reset a game to `0.1.0` and break
  tag↔version correlation. *Mitigation:* preserve is read-then-write inside
  `scaffoldGameRepo` with an integration test on a temp repo that has an existing
  version; unreadable/missing `package.json` falls back to the `0.1.0` baseline.
- **Risk — tests only assert rendered strings** (the existing test's weakness) so the
  real write path stays unguarded. *Mitigation:* AC4 requires integration-level
  coverage of the write path.
- **Risk — scope creep into release tooling.** "Fix the version" invites touching the
  ship skill, CI, or renumbering every game. *Mitigation:* Q3 decision constrains scope
  to the scaffold seeding path; any additional leak found is a follow-up work item.
- **Assumption — `0.1.0` baseline is acceptable before any release exists** (producer
  decision Q1); the first release from a new game therefore tags `v0.1.1` after the
  ship patch bump. Documented rather than special-cased.
- **Assumption — leaving existing versions in place is safe** (producer decision Q2):
  released `main-street` tags `v0.1.18`–`v0.1.21` stay valid; games diverge from the
  engine's numbering at their next release.
- **Assumption — no other core-version coupling exists** (producer decision Q3): the
  ship bump path reads the invoking repo's `package.json`; verified, not modified.

## Related work

### Automated report (find-related)

- **CG-0MSQBQSCX006R02B** — CLI draft-release script (code + docs) (completed)
- **CG-0MM1OQ5U80HVOPKJ** — Inconsistent move validation patterns across games (completed, tangential)
- **CG-0MSQ6MV7N0085V9R** — Local skill: promote Windows Setup artifact to GitHub release (operator-approved) (completed)
- Repository file matches: `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (generic keyword matches)

### Manually linked context

- **CG-0MR89YKN0000FK5W** — Add game version to menu screen and Main Street settings panel (completed): established the version display surface that makes the coupling visible.
- **CG-0MUI9K4F8009DYJL** — Add an ALPHA banner and version number to all game screens (completed): same display surface.
- **CG-0MRZ35LK80064WIS** / **CG-0MRZ0YNCO003J5CN** — CI-3 release checklist (completed): release-cadence context.
- Source: `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` in `../tce-main-street` (engine pin vs dev sync — the only other engine/game coupling data).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 — Initial version baseline for a brand-new game repo

**Question:** When the scaffold creates a **new** game repo (no prior `package.json`), should the game start at `0.1.0`, `0.0.0`, or another baseline?
**Recommended:** `0.1.0` — matches the existing `0.1.x` convention, gives a sensible first release (`v0.1.1`) without implying engine compatibility.
**Answer (producer):** `0.1.0`. Source: interactive reply (2026-10-21).

### Q2 — Existing game repos: renumber now vs leave in place

**Question:** Should existing sibling game repos (currently core-derived: 0.1.17, or 0.1.21 for `main-street`/`the-rising`) be renumbered as part of this work, or left at their current numbers and decoupled from here?
**Recommended:** leave in place — released tags (`main-street` v0.1.18–v0.1.21) already exist; renumbering would orphan tag/version correlation for little benefit.
**Answer (producer):** "as recommended" — leave in place. Source: interactive reply (2026-10-21).

### Q3 — Scope of the version leak

**Question:** Intake identified the root cause as `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` `renderPackageJson()` stamping the core manifest version into game `package.json` (pinned by `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` asserting `pkg.version === '9.9.9'`). Are other paths in scope — e.g. a release accidentally run from the core checkout, or the distribution/launcher build stamping the core version onto games?
**Recommended:** scaffold seeding + test/doc updates only (the ship `bump-version.js` already reads the invoking repo's own `package.json` via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`), with the ship path verified rather than modified.
**Answer (producer):** "as recommended" — scaffold seeding + tests/docs only; verify the ship path. Source: interactive reply (2026-10-21).

> Research note for Q3: inspected `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js`
> (`PKG_PATH = resolve(REPO_ROOT, 'package.json')`, `REPO_ROOT = git rev-parse --show-toplevel`),
> `merge-dev-to-main.sh` (same repo-local bump), `scripts/engine-sync.mjs` (pins a commit SHA in
> `configs/engine-pin.json`, no version), and each game's generated `vite.config.ts`
> (`__APP_VERSION__` from the game's own `package.json`) — no additional version-leak path found.
data.title: Cutting a release from a game uses the TCE version number

data.comment: Producer answers received (2026-10-21): **Q1** = `0.1.0` baseline for a newly scaffolded game repo; **Q2** = leave existing game repo versions in place (decouple going forward, no renumbering); **Q3** = scope limited to the scaffold seeding path + tests/docs, with the ship `bump-version.js` path verified (it already reads the invoking repo's own `package.json`) rather than modified. Brief updated; ACs finalised.
